name: narrow_range_breakout_5s_2
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: NR7 bars (narrowest range in 7 bars) on 1-min data indicate energy coiling before an expansion. When a stock prints an NR7 bar in the context of declining ATR and above-average volume, the next breakout direction tends to be the prevailing trend direction. This is a volatility-expansion trade: low-vol periods are followed by high-vol periods (mean reversion of volatility). Edge persists because most traders use NR7 on daily bars; on 1-min it's underexplored and more frequent.
mechanism: Consolidation periods accumulate resting orders above resistance and below support. A breakout triggers these resting orders as stop-losses and breakout entries fire simultaneously. The resulting order flow imbalance overwhelms the resting liquidity, and market makers widen spreads in the breakout direction, accelerating the move.

exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside NR7 range

weaknesses: NR7 on 1-min is frequent but many signals are in low-volume dead zones (lunch hour)
False breakouts: tight range breaks, reverses, and stops you out on the opposite side
Using NR7 bar range as stop can be extremely tight (< 5 bps), leading to noise-triggered stops
prior_art: NR7 (Tony Crabel) — originally daily; adapted here for 1-min intraday
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
